msg_content_badge_title.message: You have listened to this song $1 $2
msg_content_badge_title.description: Tooltip on the play-count badge in the YouTube Music player bar. $1 is the play count as a bare number and $2 is the already-localized plural noun for it ("1 play", "5 plays") - the two are kept apart because the number is rendered in its own styled element. Treat $2 as a finished noun phrase.

msg_content_badge_play_one.description: Singular noun shown beside the play count in the player-bar badge. Singular form of the counted "play". Deliberately carries no number: the count is a separate DOM element. French selects this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_content_badge_play_zero.description: Plural noun shown beside the play count in the player-bar badge, form selected at zero by pt_BR. It uses the plural because the player-bar count reads as "0 plays"; if your language treats zero as a distinct form, use it here. No number is included in this string.

msg_content_badge_play_other.description: Plural noun shown beside the play count in the player-bar badge. Carries no number - the count is a separate DOM element. en, de, es, it and fr all select this form for two or more plays.

msg_content_count_play_one.description: Counted number of listening plays, singular. $1 is the play count. Used inside longer sentences where the noun has to agree with the number, so it must work as a phrase on its own.

msg_content_count_play_zero.description: Counted number of listening plays, form selected at zero by pt_BR. $1 is the play count. pt_BR ships this form even where the plural category for zero has been dropped from CLDR, so "0 plays" reads naturally.

msg_content_count_play_other.description: Counted number of listening plays, plural. $1 is the play count. en, de, es, it and fr all select this form for two or more plays. In music contexts "play" means one complete listen to a song, not a partial or a stream.

msg_content_count_new_play_one.description: Count of plays newly imported by a history sync, singular. $1 is the number of new plays. This is the "new" counterpart of msg_content_count_play and appears only in sync-result messages.

msg_content_count_new_play_zero.description: Count of plays newly imported by a history sync, form selected at zero by pt_BR. $1 is the number of new plays.

msg_content_count_new_play_other.description: Count of plays newly imported by a history sync, plural. $1 is the number of new plays. en, de, es, it and fr select this form for two or more.

msg_content_count_song_one.description: Counted number of songs, singular. $1 is the song count. Used inside the history scanner's progress sentence. French selects this form for 0 as well as 1, so it must read correctly at zero.

msg_content_count_song_zero.description: Counted number of songs, form selected at zero by pt_BR. $1 is the song count.

msg_content_count_song_other.description: Counted number of songs, plural. $1 is the song count. Here "song" means an entry in the YouTube Music listening history.

msg_content_scanner_title.description: Title of the history-scanner overlay the extension injects onto the YouTube Music History page. Keep it short: it is the overlay's header, next to a logo. This is the extension's own feature name, not a translated brand - do NOT use the product name as a substitute.

msg_content_scanner_metric_label.description: Caption above the running counter in the history-scanner overlay. The number under it is how many songs the last sync imported.

msg_content_scanner_ready.message: Ready to sync your listening history.
msg_content_scanner_ready.description: Status line of the history-scanner overlay while it is idle and no sync has been started. A full sentence with a full stop.

msg_content_scanner_force_rescan.message: Re-scan full history from the beginning
msg_content_scanner_force_rescan.description: Label of the checkbox in the history-scanner overlay. Checking it ignores the stored sync position and walks the entire listening history again.

msg_content_scanner_start_sync.description: Label of the main button in the history-scanner overlay. The play triangle glyph is added by the code and is not part of this string, so do not translate it - but it also does not need a verb; "Sync" alone is acceptable.

msg_content_scanner_in_progress.description: Label the history-scanner overlay's start button takes while a sync is running. Keep the trailing ellipsis: it signals that the button is temporarily busy.

msg_content_scanner_minimize.description: Tooltip on the X button of the history-scanner overlay, in its expanded state. The button collapses the overlay rather than closing it.

msg_content_scanner_restore.description: Tooltip on the history-scanner overlay's collapse button while the overlay is minimized.

msg_content_scanner_toggle_minimize.description: Tooltip on the header title of the history-scanner overlay, which is clickable and expands the overlay again after it has been minimized.

msg_content_scan_scanning_history.description: Status line of the history-scanner overlay when a scan starts and there is no stored sync position to compare against, so the whole history is being walked. Full sentence with a trailing ellipsis.

msg_content_scan_checking_since.description: Status line of the history-scanner overlay when a scan starts from a stored sync position. $1 is the title of the most recently synced song, as it appears on YouTube Music - it is remote data, inserted as plain text inside the quotes, and may itself contain quotation marks. Full sentence with a trailing ellipsis.

msg_content_scan_boundary_progress.message: Scanning history... Loaded $1. Looking for sync boundary...
msg_content_scan_boundary_progress.description: Status line of the history-scanner overlay shown on each tick while the scanner scrolls the History page looking for the position where the last sync stopped. $1 arrives already pluralized, e.g. "57 songs". Treat $1 as a finished phrase. Three clauses, each with an ellipsis, matching the three stages of the scan.

msg_content_scan_saving.description: Status line of the history-scanner overlay while the plays found by a scan are being written to storage. $1 arrives already pluralized, e.g. "12 plays". Treat $1 as a finished phrase. Full sentence with a trailing ellipsis.

msg_content_scan_success.description: Bolded lead-in of the history-scanner overlay's success status line, followed by a sentence saying how much was synced. Standalone fragment - no verb, no trailing punctuation beyond the exclamation mark.

msg_content_scan_synced.description: Success status line of the history-scanner overlay when a sync finished normally. $1 arrives already pluralized, e.g. "12 new plays". Treat $1 as a finished phrase. Full sentence with a full stop.

msg_content_scan_synced_reason.description: Success status line of the history-scanner overlay when the sync finished with something worth explaining - it hit the history limit, walked the whole list, or the page was left mid-scan. $1 arrives already pluralized ("12 new plays"); $2 is an already-localized short phrase explaining why, e.g. "Reached the 200-song history limit." Treat both as finished sentences and keep the two-sentence shape.

msg_content_scan_up_to_date.message: All caught up! No new plays found.
msg_content_scan_up_to_date.description: Status line of the history-scanner overlay when a sync ran and the listening history contains nothing newer than the last sync. Full sentence with a full stop.

msg_content_scan_empty_history.description: Status line of the history-scanner overlay when a scan found nothing at all and there was no previous sync to compare against. Full sentence with a full stop. Note this says "tracks" rather than "songs" for variety with the other scanner strings; keep the distinction if your language makes it.

msg_content_scan_failed.description: Error status line of the history-scanner overlay. $1 is the underlying failure text from the extension's background process - an exception message, not a translatable sentence, so it is left in English inside the localized frame. Do not try to translate $1.
